input.question: A power generation facility has the following systems: (1) SCADA system controlling turbine operations, (2) corporate email server, (3) historian database collecting sensor data from turbines, (4) HR payroll system, (5) distributed control system (DCS) managing plant operations. Classify each system as IT or OT based on the CCoP 2.0 §1.2.1 definitions of “information technology” and “operational technology”.

ground_truth.expected_label: OT: SCADA, DCS, historian; IT: email server, HR payroll
ground_truth.expected_response: Based on the CCoP 2.0 §1.2.1 definitions of “information technology” and “operational technology” and the §10.1.1 OT-CII scope: the SCADA system and the DCS are OT systems, as the OT definition expressly covers supervisory control and data acquisition systems and distributed control systems used to monitor and/or control physical processes. The corporate email server and HR payroll system are IT systems, used for storing, processing and sending business information. The historian database is also an OT system: CCoP 2.0 expressly treats historians as OT assets, listing “OT historians” among the servers that form part of OT CII (§5.9.1(e)). CCoP 2.0 does not define a 'hybrid' IT/OT category; while a historian bridges OT data collection and IT-style analysis, it is classified as OT under the Code.

key_facts.fact: OT systems control or monitor physical processes and industrial operations, expressly including SCADA and distributed control systems (DCS)
IT systems are used for storing, accessing, processing, analysing and sending information (e.g., email, HR, payroll)
CCoP 2.0 treats historians as OT assets, listing “OT historians” among the servers forming part of OT CII; it defines no 'hybrid' IT/OT category
Section 10 provides OT-specific security requirements recognising the different operational characteristics of OT CII

forbidden_claims: All systems in a power plant are OT because they support critical infrastructure
Historian databases are pure IT systems with no OT considerations
hallucination_patterns: Claiming CCoP 2.0 defines specific percentage thresholds for hybrid classification
Inventing a formal certification process for IT vs OT determination
